artboards.title: D · gradient stops at the card, steep fan

annotations.text:
A · Sketch grid — the attached sketch, literally.
Two by two at every width, screenshots tilted and broken out of the card top. Reads as a toy shelf.
Tradeoff: at 390px the two-up cards leave ~150px of text width, so the blurbs have to be short — that is the least SEO copy of the three.

B · Marquee row — four abreast, editorial hero.
Left-aligned hero so the h1 and the paragraph read as one block; cards straight-on and equal weight.
Tradeoff: four equal cards say all four tools are equally real. Three of them are not.

C · Featured — the shipped tool leads.
The dex builder gets a split hero card with a real screenshot and a solid CTA; the other three sit in a supporting row.
Tradeoff: it buries the league builder, which is the tool with a settled spec and the next page to rank.

SEO structure, same in all three:
· h1 carries "make your own Pokédex" plus region and league.
· Each card is an <h2> that exactly matches its slug: /custom-pokedex-builder, /pokemon-league-builder, /favorite-pokemon-picker.
· The footer repeats the four links as anchor text.
Watch out: making / a router moves the dex builder off the URL that ranks today (~pos 7.8 for "pokedex builder").

D · Poster cards — proportions measured off your PowerPoint. Against a 315x161 red card: card height 0.51 of its width, phone 0.53 of the card width, top overhang 0.47 of the card height, left overhang 0.063 of the card width, front phone inset 0.098 of the card width. The back phone sits about 0.05 of the card height LOWER than the front and roughly 4 degrees counter-clockwise against the front's 2.5. Gradient covers about 0.67 of the card height.
A and B are those numbers with two and three phones. C is the same on a slightly taller card, so more screenshot shows.

D is the odd one out, and it is worth a look before you choose.
Last round you asked for the gradient to be clipped by the card outline. Your PowerPoint does the opposite: the red runs out to the artwork's own left edge, past the card, which is why there is no seam there. The two cannot both hold at a shallow tilt — clipping the gradient to the card means the artwork has to come back inside the card before the gradient starts, and at 4 degrees it never does.
So A, B and C follow the PowerPoint: the gradient carries the back phone's rotation and ends where the artwork ends. D clips it to the card instead, and pays for it with a much steeper fan (-11 and -6). Pick whichever edge you prefer.

The other two widths, both using permutation A. Desktop is the four mobile cards side by side, not a two-by-two.
Swap in whichever permutation you pick and these follow.
